title: Double hamburger on white bun, 2 small patties

content.title: About
content.content: The double hamburger consists of two small beef patties placed between a split white bun. The patties are made from 100 % beef, lightly seasoned with salt and pepper, while the bun is soft and lightly toasted. It is usually served with lettuce, a tomato slice, pickles and a sauce of choice.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Double hamburgers are often offered in fast‑food combos as a heartier alternative to a single patty burger.
A white bun provides a neutral base that lets the flavor of the patties and sauces shine.
Two small patties contain roughly half the fat of one large patty of the same total weight.
Traditionally the patties are grilled, giving them a characteristic smoky aroma.
In some countries the double hamburger is considered a “starter” for those who prefer a larger meal.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: Beef patties are a rich source of complete protein, essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Iron and zinc
items.content: Red meat provides heme iron and zinc, which support immune function and metabolism.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef contains vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, important for energy production.

items.title: Moderate fat content
items.content: Two small patties contain less saturated fat than one large patty, which can be a healthier option when monitoring fat intake.

items.title: Balanced carbohydrate source
items.content: The white bun supplies quick‑digesting carbs that give an immediate energy boost.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: Despite the small patties, a double hamburger can contain 500–700 kcal, so it should be accounted for in daily energy balance.

items.title: Saturated fat and cholesterol
items.content: Beef contains saturated fats and cholesterol, which may affect blood lipid levels if consumed in excess.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Sauces and seasonings can add significant sodium, which is a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The white bun typically contains wheat, so people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity should choose a gluten‑free alternative.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the burger hot, split the bun, place the patties, lettuce, tomato slice, pickles and your preferred sauce. It can be eaten with hands, or with a knife and fork if preferred.

content.title: Storage
content.content: A double hamburger is best enjoyed immediately. If you need to store it, wrap tightly in foil or place in an airtight container in the refrigerator, where it stays fresh for up to 24 hours. Reheat in an oven or on a grill to keep the bun from becoming soggy.
